# Diagnostics

<!-- Generated by DiagnosticReferenceTest from the Kotlin source: edit the KDoc, then run ./gradlew updateReference. -->

`MeshLink.diagnostics` emits each event below as a `DiagnosticEvent`. A code never changes meaning and is never reused, and its anchor here is the code in lower case. Each event's `toString()` shows its code, its name, its fields and its count; no field holds a key, a payload, a NodeId or a Bluetooth address. A peer appears as a `PeerRef` and a link whose peer is not yet known as a `LinkRef`; both change on every `start()`.

Repeats of a code for the same peer or link within 10 s arrive as one event whose `count` says how many it stands for. A collector that falls 256 events behind loses the oldest, then gets `ML7001`. See [Configuration](configuration.md#diagnosticsdebug) for `diagnostics.debug`.

## Severities

- `Debug`: Detail for investigations; emitted only with `DiagnosticsBuilder.debug` on.
- `Info`: A state change.
- `Warning`: Degraded, but working.
- `Error`: A feature is not working.

## ML1001

`DiagnosticEvent.Started`, severity `Info`: The node started with `profile` and `preset`.

- Cause: the app called `MeshLink.start` on a stopped node.
- Fix: none needed.
- Related: `MeshLinkConfig.securityProfile`, `MeshLinkConfig.preset`.
- Symptom: none.

Fields:

- `profile` (`SecurityProfile`): The node's security profile.
- `preset` (`Preset`): The node's preset.

## ML1002

`DiagnosticEvent.Stopped`, severity `Info`: The node stopped for `reason`.

- Cause: the app called `MeshLink.stop` or `MeshLink.resetIdentity` on a started node.
- Fix: none needed.
- Related: `MeshLink.state`.
- Symptom: none.

Fields:

- `reason` (`Stopped.Reason`): Why the node stopped.

`Stopped.Reason` values:

- `Requested`: The app called `MeshLink.stop`.
- `IdentityReset`: The app called `MeshLink.resetIdentity`.

## ML1003

`DiagnosticEvent.UnsecuredProfile`, severity `Warning`: The node started in `SecurityProfile.Unsecured`, on every start: anyone in radio range can read, forge and replay its traffic.

- Cause: the configuration chose `SecurityProfile.Unsecured`.
- Fix: choose `SecurityProfile.Classical` or `SecurityProfile.PostQuantum` unless every payload is public anyway.
- Related: `MeshLinkConfig.securityProfile`.
- Symptom: none.

## ML3003

`DiagnosticEvent.ConnectFailed`, severity `Warning`: A connect as central on `link` failed for `reason`. `attempt` counts from 1; a `Reason.Transient` failure is retried up to 3 times (spec `connect-retries`).

- Cause: the peer moved out of range or stopped advertising, or the platform failed the connect; Android reports GATT status 133 or 147 as `Reason.Transient`, often on a first connect.
- Fix: transient failures retry by themselves. If every connect fails, move the phones closer and turn Bluetooth off and on.
- Related: spec `connect-retries`.
- Symptom: peers not found.

Fields:

- `link` (`LinkRef`): The link the connect was for.
- `reason` (`ConnectFailed.Reason`): Why the connect failed.
- `attempt` (`Int`): The attempt that failed, from 1.

`ConnectFailed.Reason` values:

- `InvalidArgument`: The platform rejected an argument; a MeshLink defect.
- `PeerUnreachable`: The peer is out of range or no longer advertising.
- `CapabilityMissing`: The peer serves no MeshLink capability, so it is not a MeshLink node.
- `LinkClosed`: The link closed before the connect finished.
- `Unsupported`: The platform has no radio MeshLink can use.
- `RadioError`: The platform radio refused or failed the connect, for example out of resources.
- `Transient`: A cause that often clears on retry, such as Android GATT status 133 or 147.

## ML3004

`DiagnosticEvent.LinkCapReached`, severity `Debug`: The node refused a bearer, as it holds `cap` links: its link budget, or the radio's cap on links as peripheral.

- Cause: many peers in range; expected in a dense mesh.
- Fix: none needed; the node links to other peers as its links close.
- Related: `MeshLinkConfig.density`.
- Symptom: peers not found.

Fields:

- `cap` (`Int`): The cap the node holds.

## ML3005

`DiagnosticEvent.BearerFallback`, severity `Info`: An L2CAP CoC channel to `peer` failed to open for `reason`, so the link stays on GATT (spec "Bearer switch").

- Cause: the platform or the peer refused the channel.
- Fix: none needed; GATT carries the same traffic more slowly. If it happens with every peer, turn `MeshLinkConfigBuilder.l2capUpgrade` off.
- Related: `MeshLinkConfig.l2capUpgrade`.
- Symptom: messages not delivered.

Fields:

- `peer` (`PeerRef`): The peer of the link.
- `reason` (`BearerFallback.Reason`): Why the channel failed to open.

`BearerFallback.Reason` values:

- `InvalidArgument`: The platform rejected an argument; a MeshLink defect.
- `PeerUnreachable`: The peer is out of range.
- `LinkClosed`: The link closed before the channel opened.
- `RadioError`: The platform radio refused or failed the channel.
- `Transient`: A cause that often clears on retry.

## ML3007

`DiagnosticEvent.UnknownLinkFrameDropped`, severity `Debug`: An open link dropped a link-local frame of `type` it doesn't handle: an unknown type, or a `REKEY` on an `Unsecured` link. The link stays open.

- Cause: the peer runs a newer MeshLink version, or is faulty.
- Fix: none needed. If it repeats, update both apps to the same MeshLink version.
- Related: spec "Link frames".
- Symptom: none.

Fields:

- `type` (`Int`): The frame's type byte, `0x00`–`0x3F`.

## ML4001

`DiagnosticEvent.HandshakeFailed`, severity `Warning`: The handshake on `link` failed for `reason`, and the link closed.

- Cause: `Reason.Timeout`: the peer moved away or is overloaded. `Reason.Decrypt`: the peer uses another security profile, mesh ID or mesh key. `Reason.Certificate`: the peer's certificate is invalid or expired, often a wrong clock. `Reason.Protocol`: an incompatible or faulty peer.
- Fix: give every phone of the mesh the same security profile, mesh ID and mesh key, and a correct clock.
- Related: `MeshLinkConfig.securityProfile`, `MeshLinkConfig.meshId`, `MeshLinkConfig.meshKey`.
- Symptom: peers not found.

Fields:

- `link` (`LinkRef`): The link whose handshake failed.
- `reason` (`HandshakeFailed.Reason`): What failed.

`HandshakeFailed.Reason` values:

- `Timeout`: Not complete within `handshake-timeout` after the bearer opened.
- `Decrypt`: A handshake message failed to decrypt or carried an unusable key. Another security profile, mesh ID or mesh key all fail this way.
- `Certificate`: The peer's certificate was missing, invalid, expired, or bound another key.
- `Protocol`: An unexpected, malformed or version-changing handshake frame.

## ML4002

`DiagnosticEvent.HandshakeLimitDropped`, severity `Warning`: A handshake broke a denial-of-service bound, `limit`, so the bearer closed without a reply (spec "Handshake limits").

- Cause: many phones connecting at once, or a peer opening handshakes faster than allowed.
- Fix: none needed; honest peers succeed on a later attempt.
- Related: spec "Handshake limits".
- Symptom: peers not found.

Fields:

- `limit` (`HandshakeLimitDropped.Limit`): The bound the handshake broke.

`HandshakeLimitDropped.Limit` values:

- `PerBearer`: A second handshake on one bearer (`handshake-half-open-per-link`).
- `Global`: More than `handshake-half-open-global` handshakes at once.
- `NeighborInterval`: A new handshake from one address within `handshake-neighbor-interval`.

## ML7001

`DiagnosticEvent.DiagnosticsDropped`, severity `Warning`: This collector fell `dropped` events behind, so its oldest events were dropped. Each collector buffers 256 events.

- Cause: the collector does slow work for each event.
- Fix: collect on a fast path and move slow work elsewhere.
- Related: `MeshLink.diagnostics`.
- Symptom: none.

Fields:

- `dropped` (`Int`): How many events this collector lost.

## ML7002

`DiagnosticEvent.ReadTrackingEvicted`, severity `Info`: The oldest delivered message awaiting a read receipt was forgotten, as more than 1,000 were tracked; its status stays `DeliveryStatus.Delivered`.

- Cause: the app sends many messages that request read receipts, and their recipients don't read them.
- Fix: request read receipts only for messages whose reading matters.
- Related: `ReadReceiptsBuilder.requestByDefault`.
- Symptom: messages not delivered.

Fields:

- `messageId` (`ByteArray`): A copy of the forgotten message's `message_id`.
